 Two Senoia residents are among three men charged in a federal tax refund fraud scheme that allegedly resulted in the theft of more than $74 million from the U.S. Treasury.
 Gustavo Rojano Salazar, 41, and Andres Huerta Rendon, 43, were living in Senoia at the time of their arrests, according to the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Georgia.
 The third defendant, Gustavo Rojano Salazar’s brother, Gabriel Rojano Salazar, 49, also lived in the Atlanta area.
 The three men, all Mexican nationals, were arrested Oct. 14 after a federal grand jury indictment alleging they took part in a yearslong scheme involving fraudulent tax returns, false identities and money laundering.
 According to federal prosecutors, the defendants and others cashed more than 16,000 fraudulent tax refund checks between January 2019 and October 2026, collecting more than $74 million.
 Investigators allege the defendants obtained Mexican identification documents in the names of other people and used them to request Individual Taxpayer Identification Numbers, or ITINs, from the Internal Revenue Service.
 Once the numbers were issued, the defendants allegedly prepared and filed fraudulent federal income tax returns in the names of the ITIN holders.
 The returns included false information about tax withholdings and other financial details that generated refunds, according to prosecutors.
 Federal authorities said the refund checks were mailed to post office boxes the defendants controlled.
 The checks were then allegedly cashed at a metro Atlanta check-cashing business, where the defendants received large amounts of cash.
 “These aliens allegedly engaged in a yearslong scheme to steal over $74 million from the American people by filing fraudulent tax returns,” U.S. Attorney Theodore S. Hertzberg said in announcing the charges Oct. 14. “My office is committed to prosecuting and punishing those who steal or fabricate identities to plunder public coffers.”
 A federal grand jury returned an indictment Oct. 6 charging all three defendants with conspiracy to commit mail and wire fraud, mail fraud and conspiracy to commit concealment money laundering.
 Gustavo Rojano Salazar and Gabriel Rojano Salazar face additional charges of making false statements on immigration forms. Prosecutors allege they submitted immigration applications falsely stating they had never committed a crime.
 Each defendant faces up to 20 years in prison on each fraud and money laundering conspiracy count. The Rojano Salazar brothers also face up to 15 years on each immigration count.
 The defendants appeared before Chief U.S. Magistrate Judge Justin S. Anand on Oct. 14 after their arrests and were ordered held in the custody of the U.S. Marshals Service pending further proceedings.
 The case is being investigated by IRS Criminal Investigation, the U.S. Postal Inspection Service and Homeland Security Investigations.
 Assistant U.S. Attorney Kelly K. Connors and Senior Litigation Counsel Michael C. Boteler of the Justice Department’s Fraud Division Tax Section are prosecuting the case.
 The charges are allegations, and all three defendants are presumed innocent unless proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt.
